plugins.description: This is a limiter with an attack time of 5ms. It adds just over 5ms of latency to the input signal, but it guarantees that there will be no signals over the limit, and tries to get the minimum amount of distortion

plugins.name: Fast overdrive
plugins.description: A simple overdrive. Compresses the extreme peaks to make a sound similar to an overdriven amplifier.

plugins.name: Flanger
plugins.description: A digital flanger implementation. Uses a novel zero excursion, controlled bandwidth modulation function, which should make the modulation less repetitive and noticeable. This effect is similar in character to a phaser (see section \ref{lfoPhaser}). The main difference is that a phaser sounds more regular and stable.

plugins.name: Foldover distortion

plugins.name: Retro Flanger
plugins.description: A model of someone flanging the input. Models the tape saturation effects, and frequency smear of a manual flanger. The results are a slightly distorted, but more subtle flanger sound that you get from a normal digital flanger.

plugins.name: Reverse Delay (5s max)
plugins.description:
A reverse delay not really modelled on any existing one.  You'll want to set
         the Crossfade Samples parameter to something reasonably small (but more than 20)
         for most applications, but you can try larger values if you start getting clicking

plugins.name: Simple amplifier
plugins.description: Steve Harris SWH LADSPA plugin set.

plugins.name: Single band parametric
plugins.description: A single band of a parametric filter.

plugins.name: Tape Delay Simulation
plugins.description: Correctly models the tape motion and some of the smear effect. The way the tape accelerates and decelerates gives a nicer delay effect for many purposes.

plugins.name: Triple band parametric with shelves
plugins.description: Actually five bands of eq, but the first and last are locked to shelving filters.

plugins.name: Valve saturation
plugins.description: A model of valve (tube) distortion, lacking some of the harmonics you would get in a real tube amp, but sounds good nonetheless.

plugins.name: C* AmpVTS - Idealised guitar amplification
plugins.description: Tracing the circuit stages of an idealised [resp. idolised] tube amplifier, this plugin aims to present a recreation of those features of traditional guitar amplification electronics that have proved musically useful, and to provide them with the most musical rather than the most authentic ranges of adjustment and character.

plugins.name: C* CabinetIII - Simplistic loudspeaker cabinet emulation
plugins.description: A loudspeaker cabinet emulation implemented as two sets of 31st-order IIR filters precomputed (using Prony's method) for fs of 44.1 and 48 kHz

plugins.name: C* CabinetIV - Idealised loudspeaker cabinet
plugins.description: This plugin applies an acoustic instrument body modeling technique to recreate the linear frequency response of an electric guitar amplifier's speaker cabinet. A selection of several hundred frequency response approximations of recordings from classic cabinets was narrowed down to a handful of idealised tones.

plugins.name: C* ChorusI - Mono chorus/flanger
plugins.description: A standard mono chorus with optional feedback. The parameter range suits subtle effects as well as all-out flanging.

plugins.name: C* Compress - Compressor and saturating limiter
plugins.description: This compressor has originally been designed to create more vocal-like sustain for the electric guitar without sacrificing its brightly percussive character

plugins.name: C* CompressX2 - Stereo compressor and saturating limiter
plugins.description: This stereo version of Compress applies uniform compression to both channels in proportion to their combined power.

plugins.name: C* Eq10 - 10-band equaliser
plugins.description: 10-band equaliser. A classic octave-band constant-Q second-order filter design, basically a direct digital translation of an analog original.

plugins.name: C* Eq10X2 - Stereo 10-band equaliser
plugins.description: Stereo 10-band equaliser. The controls of this stereo version of Eq apply to both channels.

plugins.name: C* Eq4p - 4-band parametric shelving equaliser
plugins.description: 4-band parametric shelving equaliser. Four adjustable biquad filters in series, in vector arithmetic implementation.  The default setup is an identity filter with a mode configuration of lowshelve, band, band, hishelve, all at zero gain.

plugins.name: C* EqFA4p - 4-band parametric eq
plugins.description: 4-band parametric eq. Four Mitra-Regalia peaking equaliser filters in series; a vector arithmetic re-implementation of Fons Adriaensens Parametric1 equaliser with minor differences

plugins.name: C* JVRev - Stanford-style reverb from STK
plugins.description: This is based on some of the famous Stanford CCRMA reverbs (NRev, KipRev) all based on the Chowning/Moorer/Schroeder reverberators, which use networks of simple allpass and comb delay filters.

plugins.name: C* Noisegate - Attenuating hum and noise
plugins.description: Attenuating hum and noise. This effect plugin attenuates the signal when it is deemed to be background noise.

plugins.name: C* PhaserII - Mono phaser
plugins.description: Mono phaser. This take on the classic effect features two modulation choices, traditional sine-based periodicity or smoothened fractal oscillation.

plugins.name: C* Plate - Versatile plate reverb
plugins.description: This is based on some of the famous Stanford CCRMA reverbs (NRev, KipRev) all based on the Chowning/Moorer/Schroeder reverberators, which use networks of simple allpass and comb delay filters.

plugins.name: C* PlateX2 - Versatile plate reverb, stereo inputs
plugins.description: This is based on some of the famous Stanford CCRMA reverbs (NRev, KipRev) all based on the Chowning/Moorer/Schroeder reverberators, which use networks of simple allpass and comb delay filters.

plugins.name: C* Scape - Stereo delay with chromatic resonances
plugins.description: Stereo delay with chromatic resonances. A stereo delay with resonant filters and fractally modulated panning. With every beat, the filter resonance frequencies are retuned to random steps on an equal-tempered chromatic scale

plugins.name: C* Spice - Not an exciter
plugins.description: Not an exciter. This effect plugin is useful when more bass register definition or more treble presence is called for and generic equalisation does not work without also emphasising noise or raising the signal's total level.  A common application is refreshing of material that has been subjected to low-fidelity analog transmission

plugins.name: C* ToneStack - Classic amplifier tone stack emulation
plugins.description: Classic amplifier tone stack emulation. All models are using the procedural implementation with continuously updated direct form II filters and sample rate independency.

plugins.name: valve preamplifier model
plugins.description: Tim Goetze's C* DSP plugin collection.

plugins.name: TAP AutoPanner
plugins.description: The AutoPanner is a very well-known effect; its hardware incarnation originates in the age of voltage controlled synthesizers. Its main use is to liven up synth tracks in the mix.

plugins.name: TAP Chorus/Flanger
plugins.description: This plugin is an implementation capable of creating traditional Chorus and Flanger effects, spiced up a bit to make use of stereo processing. It sounds best on guitar and synth tracks.

plugins.name: TAP Equalizer
plugins.description: This plugin is an 8-band equalizer with adjustable band center frequencies.

plugins.name: TAP Equalizer/BW
plugins.description: This plugin is an 8-band equalizer with adjustable band center frequencies. It allows you to make precise adjustments to the tonal coloration of your tracks.

plugins.name: TAP Fractal Doubler
plugins.description: Originally developed to do vocal doubling, this plugin is suitable for doubling tracks with vocals, acoustic/electric guitars, bass and just about any other instrument on them. The effect is created by applying small changes to the pitch and timing of the incoming signal.

plugins.name: TAP Pitch Shifter
plugins.description: This plugin gives you the opportunity to change the pitch of individual tracks or full mixes, in the range of plus/minus one octave. Audio length (tempo) is not affected by this plugin, since audio is completely resampled.

plugins.name: TAP Reflector
plugins.description: This plugin creates a psychedelic reverse audio effect. Overlapping time intervals of incoming samples are treated as blocks called 'fragments'. Each fragment is reversed in time, and faded in and out while played back to the output, hence creating a nearly constant signal level with the mixture resembling a normal reverse-played track -- with the difference that the audio actually progresses forward, only pieces of it are reversed.

plugins.name: TAP Reverberator
plugins.description: TAP Reverberator is unique among reverberators freely available on the Linux platform. It supports creating no less than 43 reverberation effects.

plugins.name: TAP Rotary Speaker
plugins.description: This plugin simulates the sound of rotating speakers. Two pairs of rotating speakers are simulated, each pair fixed on a vertical axis, with their horns spreading the sound in opposite directions.

plugins.name: TAP Scaling Limiter
plugins.description: You want to maximize the loudness of your master tracks. Your drummer has the habit of playing with varying velocity. You want to squeeze high transient spikes down into the bulk of the audio. You want a limiter with transparent sound, but without distortion. This is for you, then. The unique design of this innocent looking plugin results in the ability to achieve signal level limiting without audible artifacts.

plugins.name: TAP Sigmoid Booster
plugins.description: This plugin applies a time-invariant nonlinear amplitude transfer function to the signal. Depending on the signal and the plugin settings, various related effects (compression, soft limiting, emulation of tape saturation, mild distortion) can be achieved.

plugins.name: TAP Stereo Echo
plugins.description: This plugin supports conventional mono and stereo delays, ping-pong delays and the Haas effect (also known as Cross Delay Stereo). A relatively simple yet quite effective plugin.

plugins.name: TAP Tremolo
plugins.description: TAP = Tom's Audio Processing LADSPA plugins.

plugins.name: TAP TubeWarmth
plugins.description: TAP TubeWarmth adds the character of vacuum tube amplification to your audio tracks by emulating the sonically desirable nonlinear characteristics of triodes. In addition, this plugin also supports emulating analog tape saturation.

plugins.name: TAP Vibrato
plugins.description: This plugin modulates the pitch of its input signal with a low-frequency sinusoidal signal. It is useful for guitar and synth tracks, and it can also come handy if a strange effect is needed.

plugins.name: Gx_expander
plugins.description: The expander is a compressor in reverse. There are two types of expander. In some, signals above the threshold remain at unity gain whereas signals below the threshold are reduced in gain, whereas in others the signal above the threshold also has the gain increased. Therefore you can use an expander as a noise reduction unit. Set the threshold to be just below the level of the player when playing. When the player stops the signal will fall below this threshold and the signal is reduced in gain thus reducing the noise or spill.
